objective: Measure whether perspective and revelation claims become asserted only when the narrative evidence available at that checkpoint supports them, while preserving intentional omniscience, unresolved interpretation and human review.
acceptance: Knowledge-before-exposure false positives are measured independently of end-of-passage accuracy.
Narrator identity and focalizer identity are independently representable and conflation is measurable.
Intentional omniscience permits multiple supported focalizers rather than forcing one permanent center.
Open questions and delayed revelations cannot be counted as correctly closed before the supporting checkpoint.
Constitutively subjective perspective interpretations retain an explicit human-review path.
No new perspective taxonomy is introduced unless an observed case cannot be represented by the existing semantics.
failure_rule: A later correct answer does not erase an earlier unsupported ASSERTED claim. Premature certainty remains failure evidence.

completion_delta.before: Generic extraction scoring can evaluate final labels, confidence and ambiguity but not evidence-timing errors across narrative checkpoints.
completion_delta.after: Perspective/revelation evaluation can distinguish eventual correctness from premature certainty, narrator/focalizer conflation, premature question closure and intentional omniscience while preserving human-review requirements.
